title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.15 is the second re-check of recent fixes. It closes the holes the first re-check left: a library component still offered for removal under another label, Remove All Unused Resource Keys still reading the disk, an Rx pairing that missed `?.dispose()`, a KDoc escape that broke the deprecation blockquote, and a qualified-R rule that had gone too far and would have hidden a module's own `R`.

highlights.title: Library components left alone
highlights.description: The 1.42.14 change stopped calling androidx.startup.InitializationProvider "class not found" but then judged it "never referenced" and still offered its removal. A class outside the workspace's packages is simply fine now.

highlights.title: Qualified R, the right way round
highlights.description: The 1.42.14 rule excluded every qualified R, which would have hidden a module's own com.app.feature.R.string.x from folding, hovers and Go to Definition. Only android.R, androidx R and Material's R are excluded, and on every surface, not just the diagnostics.

highlights.title: Rx pairing and KDoc, finished
highlights.description: disposable?.dispose() and val d: Disposable = …subscribe( pair correctly, and the KDoc escape no longer turns the deprecation blockquote into a literal ">". Remove All Unused Resource Keys reads open editors like its symbol sibling.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Shows a disabled "(offline)" placeholder in the Logcat device picker while the host's device is away, instead of displaying the wrong device as selected.
Treats case RED, GREEN -> as a switch arm, keeps '{' and @file:Suppress("unused(") from breaking signature reads and import bounds, and disposes the online-docs listener with the extension.
